title: Farm Environmental Passport — agent skill (preview)
description:
An agent skill that builds an independent environmental passport for one specific farm: what enters the farm, what has been measured and by what method, what has never been measured, and which sample to take first. PFAS screening is the first module; the same construction covers water, nutrients, soil, livestock, other contaminants, climate risk, ponds and biodiversity.

Preview. The method is demonstrated on a synthetic dairy farm in Delaware County, New York; every laboratory value in the examples is invented and labelled as such, while the thresholds, the structure and the calculations are real. The skill has not yet been validated on a real farm. The passport is screening and expert opinion, not a compliance determination, a laboratory report or medical advice.

Contents: the skill (SKILL.md), an indicator catalogue of 113 indicators, threshold packs for New York / US federal and the European Union stored with legal status and date, dose scenarios including an infant fed formula prepared with well water and a young child, Monte Carlo uncertainty and value-of-information sampling, a NASA remote-sensing layer, worked examples in English and Russian, READMEs in English, Japanese and Russian, and a test suite (34 tests).

Method: Baldanova R. (2026). Farm Environmental Passport: a status-and-gap method for screening the environmental pathways of a single farm, with PFAS as the first module. Methods note. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24017216
